claims.text: Introducing Mo, Nb, Ta, and W in a specific ratio can improve the high-temperature mechanical capability of an HEA.
The refractory-element intervention can limit alloy density.
The refractory-element intervention can preserve room-temperature performance.
The claimed benefit should hold at 800–1000 °C under applied stress.
The claimed benefit should hold over a stress range of 100–500 MPa.
Introducing the refractory elements will form a stable solid-solution phase.
Introducing the refractory elements will refine the grain structure.
The refractory elements enhance the thermal stability of the HEA.
Enhanced thermal stability reduces the formation of detrimental phases.
Relative to conventional HEAs without refractory-element additions, the intervention will improve high-temperature strength.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will improve creep resistance.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will improve oxidation resistance.
The optimal refractory-element ratio and the governing high-temperature mechanisms remain unknown.

contradictions.description: The intervention is repeatedly described as using a 'specific ratio,' but no ratio is given and the uncertainty field states that the optimal ratio is unknown.

The mechanism field confidently attributes the benefit to enhanced thermal stability and suppression of detrimental phases, while the uncertainty field says the specific governing mechanisms are unknown.
